NDT software in Toronto: one system for a spread-out GTA operation

An NDT company in Toronto needs software that holds together crews spread across the GTA, clients in very different sectors and a certification matrix that changes every month. The Atlantis ERP solution is a fully customized ERP for NDT and inspection companies. It connects reports, technician certificates, equipment calibration, crew dispatch, quoting and invoicing, and it is set up and supported by Atlantis NDT, whose founder is an ASNT NDT Level III.

Toronto's inspection market is broader than any other Canadian city's. Within a couple of hours' drive you have nuclear generation at Pickering and Darlington and, further north, Bruce Power's site on Lake Huron; transit and highway construction; high-rise and structural steel work; aerospace maintenance around Pearson; pipelines and gas utilities; food and pharmaceutical plants; and hundreds of fabrication shops across Mississauga, Brampton, Vaughan and Durham Region. A single Toronto NDT company might be doing structural weld UT on a downtown tower in the morning, MT on a fabricator's shop floor after lunch, and a night shift of PT at an industrial plant in Scarborough.

That mix is why generic tools break down. Each client has its own report format, code and certification requirement. Each trip across the 401 costs time, so good dispatch actually matters. Below, each Atlantis ERP app is applied to that Toronto reality.

ERP for NDT companies in Toronto: the core apps

An ERP for NDT companies in Toronto should follow a job from the first enquiry to the paid invoice, and keep the certification and calibration evidence attached the whole way. The Atlantis ERP does this with apps designed for inspection work.

  • NDT Reports: 17 report types (UT, RT, MT, PT, VT, ECT, IRIS, PAUT, MFL, TOFD, PWHT, PMI, hardness, UT thickness, ferrite, holiday/coating and computed radiography), each numbered separately.
  • Certificates: technician certs by scheme, level and method, vision tests, exam sheets, company certifications and expiry alerts.
  • Team Assignments: dispatch workflow, availability calendar and blocking of double-booked technicians and equipment.
  • Asset Management: instruments and probes by serial number, calibration register, issue/return approval.
  • Project and Timesheets: job scope, codes, acceptance criteria, and time split by inspection, travel, standby and setup.
  • Quotations and Invoicing: NDT-aware quotes and invoices with labour, equipment and consumables subtotals.

Everything runs in the cloud, so the office in Etobicoke, the Level III working from home in Oakville and the technician in a basement parkade in North York all see the same record. The complete app list is at /erp/apps.

Technician certification tracking software for Toronto's mixed sectors

Technician certification tracking software in Toronto has to cope with clients that each want something different. The Atlantis ERP records every certificate a technician holds, including scheme, level, method, certifying body, issue, expiry and renewal dates, industry sector, OJT and training hours, and attachments. It then computes whether each one is active, expiring soon, expired or revoked.

In practice, a Toronto technician might hold:

  • CGSB certification under NRCan's ISO 9712 program for UT, MT and RT, which Canadian industrial and construction clients commonly ask for.
  • Employer certification under SNT-TC-1A for US-headquartered clients.
  • A CWB welding inspector certification to CSA W178.2 for structural steel work. It can be stored under the "other" scheme with its own dates and attachment.
  • CNSC exposure device operator certification for radiography, attached to the employee NDT profile alongside radiation safety training, badge number and medical fitness expiry.

Because the industry sector is recorded on each cert, you can tell apart a technician qualified for general industrial work from one whose file supports nuclear or aerospace assignments. Nuclear clients working under CSA N285.4 periodic inspection programs are strict about personnel qualification evidence, and the certificate register with attached exam sheets and vision tests gives you that evidence in one place.

Daily checks create warning tasks 90 days before expiry, and configurable emails go to whoever you choose. Timesheets flag time booked by a technician whose certificate is not valid. Atlantis trains to ASNT SNT-TC-1A only. The ERP records ISO 9712, PCN and CSWIP certificates but Atlantis does not deliver training for them.

Crew dispatch software for GTA traffic and multi-site days

Crew dispatch software for a Toronto NDT company earns its keep by getting the right certified technician and a calibrated kit to the right site the first time. With GTA traffic, a wasted trip can cost half a shift. The Team Assignments app moves each job through planned, dispatched, in field, submitted and closed.

Every assignment stores the site's GPS coordinates and the mobilisation and demobilisation dates. Planners see each technician's status, current assignment, utilisation and next available date. The availability calendar holds assigned, leave, training, sick and unavailable days, and overlaps are blocked. Time Off approvals feed in automatically, so a technician's booked vacation is already visible when you schedule next month's shop inspections.

Two checks matter most in Toronto:

  • No double-booking. A technician cannot be put on two overlapping jobs, and neither can an equipment serial number. That ends the familiar argument over which crew has the only TOFD setup today.
  • Calibration warning. If the flaw detector or yoke you assign is out of calibration, the planner is warned before the crew leaves the shop.

Calendar, kanban and list views suit different people in the office. Project records hold the safety induction and work permit fields many GTA construction and industrial sites require, so you know who has completed a given site's orientation. The Fleet app assigns vans to projects and drivers with dates and mileage, and records which vehicles are licensed to carry radioactive sources.

NDT reporting software for construction, nuclear and industrial clients

NDT reporting software for Toronto clients has to produce very different reports for very different reviewers, and all of them need to be traceable. The Atlantis NDT Reports app captures method-specific data and sends each report through draft, in progress, review, approved and sent, with inspector, reviewer and approver signatures.

How that plays out across GTA work:

  • Structural steel and construction. UT and MT reports with weld lines, defect type and orientation, and drawing and WPS references, so a building's steel erector, engineer and inspection agency can match each weld to the drawing.
  • Nuclear and power. UT with the probe calibration table, PAUT focal laws, TOFD, ECT and UT thickness readings by direction, with procedure and standard references recorded on every report.
  • Industrial plants. PT with method and developer, RT with source, technique, IQI type and placement, and hardness and PMI for material checks.
  • Coatings. Holiday testing reports for pipe and tank linings.

Where a third-party or authorized inspector is involved, their name and signature are captured on the report. Your company templates are versioned in Excel, Word, PDF or HTML with logo, header and footer. If a Toronto general contractor insists on its own Excel sheet, fields are mapped to cells and the template fills itself. The offline field app keeps working in underground parkades, tunnels and plant basements where there is no signal, then syncs later. For asset owners who want to see results on a 3D model, see Digital Twin Reporting.

Calibration management software for a Toronto equipment pool

Calibration management software for a busy Toronto NDT company should tell you where every instrument is, who has it and whether it is fit to use. In Asset Management, each flaw detector, PAUT unit, probe, yoke, UV lamp, densitometer and hardness tester is tracked by serial number, with assigned person, condition, asset tag, firmware, accessories and lifecycle status: new, active, in calibration, in repair, rented out, retired or disposed.

Calibration records hold the provider, certificate number, standard, range, uncertainty, accredited-lab flag, result and next due date. The certificate register stores the lab's accreditation number and the PDF, with valid, expiring or expired status and email alerts. When a nuclear or aerospace client asks for the calibration certificate behind a specific report, it takes seconds.

Issue and return go through supervisor and manager approval, and condition is recorded at both ends, so damage to a probe cable is traced to the right job. Reservations prevent clashes, and every inbound and outbound movement is logged. The maintenance log covers preventive and corrective work, probe replacement and firmware updates. Consumables such as penetrant kits, MT ink, couplant and PPE have reorder levels. The Purchase app records vendor types (OEM, dealer, calibration lab), accredited-lab status with accreditation number and expiry, and links order lines to a specific equipment serial.

Procedures and quality control for Toronto audits

Toronto NDT companies face audits from nuclear licensees, general contractors, aerospace MROs and their own ISO 9001 registrar, sometimes in the same quarter. The Procedures app keeps one controlled register for all of them: document number, revision, method, scope, material, applicable standard (such as ASME Section V or the relevant CSA standard), acceptance criteria, and body text or attached file.

The workflow runs draft, submitted, reviewed, approved and published, with rejection reasons and archiving. Prepared, reviewed and approved by are recorded with dates, approved revisions are locked, and every revision keeps a snapshot. An auditor asking which revision of your UT procedure applied to a weld inspected last March gets a straight answer. Approvers get email notifications and reminders. An AI-assisted first draft helps your Level III start a new procedure faster, but the Level III still reviews and approves it.

NCR and CAPA workflows can be configured during implementation, so that a rejected report or an audit finding becomes a tracked corrective action. Company certifications such as ISO 9001 or client-specific approvals are stored with their own alert days. For context, pressure equipment in Ontario is regulated by TSSA and radiography sources by the CNSC. The ERP keeps your evidence organised for those regimes but does not replace any regulator's or owner's program.

NDT quoting and invoicing software for Toronto clients

NDT quoting and invoicing software for Toronto has to handle everything from a one-day shop call-out to a multi-month construction contract. Quotations record job type, site, project dates and applicable codes, apply a global discount, and use NDT service products flagged by method and category. Clients receive a branded PDF, can accept and sign online, and the quote converts to a sales order.

Invoicing holds the NDT project, job or PO number, site, invoice type and industry sector in the header, with labour, equipment and consumables subtotals. Lines can show cost centre, method, equipment serial, technician, rate type, and days or hours. General contractors and plant owners in the GTA often reject invoices that don't match their PO structure. Mapping your lines to their PO and cost centres is set up during implementation.

Timesheets separate inspection, travel, standby and setup, flag billable time and apply rate multipliers for overtime and weekend work. Waiting on a crane or for a hold point to clear then gets billed instead of absorbed. HST and payment terms are configured for Ontario. Expenses captures parking, 407 tolls and per diems and re-bills them to the job. The financial dashboard shows revenue, cost of sales, gross margin, operating expenses, EBITDA and outstanding invoices over twelve months.

Inspection management software in Toronto: sales and growth

Inspection management software for a Toronto company should also help you win work, because competition across the GTA is heavy. The CRM records service line, lead source, NDT service type, industry sector, site country, and estimated technicians and days. An NDT lead score of 0 to 100 sorts leads into hot, warm, nurture and cold.

Leads can be imported from CSV, emails personalised with an AI preview, and contacts enrolled in drip sequences by service line with pause, resume and unsubscribe. AI Marketing drafts newsletters and announcements using a model that can run on your own server. Business Cards turns a photo of a card from a trade show or association meeting into a CRM lead in one click. Your company website's enquiry forms feed the CRM directly, and Surveys can collect client feedback after each job.

Dashboards put NDT KPIs next to sales: calibration due and overdue, certs expiring and expired, and issued equipment overdue for return. If you already run accounting or maintenance software, the open REST API connects to QuickBooks, NetSuite, SAP, Maximo or any system that accepts API connections, scoped per implementation.

Implementing the Atlantis ERP in Toronto

A Toronto rollout is usually staged by department, so field work never stops.

  1. Discovery. We review your sectors, report formats, certification schemes, equipment pool and how jobs flow today.
  2. Certificates and assets first. Technicians, CGSB and SNT-TC-1A certs, CWB and CNSC documents, vision tests, and every instrument with its calibration history are loaded. For many Toronto companies this alone clears up most audit stress.
  3. Dispatch and timesheets. Planners move off the whiteboard, and technicians book time on phones.
  4. Reports. Your templates and client-specific Excel formats are rebuilt, and crews start on the offline app.
  5. Quoting, invoicing and CRM. Sales and accounts come across, with HST, invoice layouts and any integration configured.
  6. Support. Atlantis NDT stays involved as you add apps.

If you develop your own technicians, the eLearning app hosts Level I to III courses, protected video lessons, quizzes and completion certificates, and the Practical NDT 3D simulator gives trainees practice before live work. Book a Toronto ERP demo and bring a real job so we can walk it through end to end.

Frequently asked questions

What is the best NDT software for a Toronto inspection company?

Look for one system covering reports, certifications, calibration, dispatch and billing. The Atlantis ERP does all of these and is configured for the mix of construction, nuclear, industrial and aerospace work typical of the GTA.

Can it hold CGSB ISO 9712 and CWB certifications together?

Yes. ISO 9712 is a built-in scheme. CWB and other certifications can be recorded under "other" with their own dates, attachments and expiry alerts.

Is it cloud NDT software?

Yes. It runs in the browser for the office, and the field app installs on phones and tablets, works offline and syncs later.

Does it support nuclear work?

It keeps the personnel qualification, calibration, procedure and report evidence that nuclear clients audit. It does not replace a licensee's own inspection program.

Can it integrate with QuickBooks or SAP?

Yes. The open REST API connects to QuickBooks, NetSuite, SAP, Maximo or any system that accepts API connections, scoped during implementation.

What does it cost?

Pricing is quote on request, based on the apps and configuration you need. Ask for a Toronto quote.

Does Atlantis provide NDT training in Toronto?

Atlantis offers NDT training based on ASNT SNT-TC-1A only. The ERP records ISO 9712, PCN and CSWIP certificates, but Atlantis does not deliver training for those schemes.
